scope: Serial engine invocation in a resident Python worker, including CLI process startup or API state creation/deletion; not end-to-end ACCIM/BESOS throughput.

cases.name: accim-custom-one-day
cases.model: Two-zone TestModel, vrf_ac, CS99, CAT80, CM3, HVACmode0, m=0.31, n=17.8; one-day weather run, no sizing-period simulation.
cases.epw: Seville.epw copied by the same fixture
cases.notes: No meter CSV emitted by either backend; ReadVarsESO reports the absent MTR. Input sample retains its known orphan IdealLoads diagnostics. Success here means matching emitted series and successful engine completion, not a warning-free model.

limitations: Five pairs per case on one workstation and one engine release; no general speedup claim or statistical significance claim.
API import/DLL initialization is reported separately; starting a new Python interpreter for every evaluation was not measured.
Both backends use exactly the same model, weather and engine flags within a case.
No concurrent simulations, memory profiling, control callbacks, PythonPlugin or interrupted-state recovery measured.
CSV checks cover emitted variable/meter time series, not arbitrary artifacts or all model/control configurations.
Raw JSON outside the repository retains input SHA256 hashes, warmup times and per-run artifact paths; times in this summary are rounded to six decimals.
